title: Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
content_c:
Search for Amelia Earhart's plane resumes after stormy weather
- Published
A search for the wreckage of Amelia Earhart's plane on a remote island in the Pacific Ocean has resumed after severe weather caused researchers to stop for several days.
A team has travelled to Nikumaroro Island, part of Kiribati, hoping to solve the mystery of the famed aviator's disappearance by investigating the so-called Taraia Object, spotted in the atoll's lagoon in aerial imagery.
The American pioneer vanished while attempting to circumnavigate the globe in 1937, spawning decades of speculation about her fate.
Rough seas and strong winds forced the team to remain on their research vessel for three days, until the weather cleared on Sunday.
"We are finally getting off the ship and able to land on Nikumaroro," Sirisha Bandla, a technology specialist who is part of the expedition, said in a video update from the deck of the Marin Mainiku.
The researchers arrived at the uninhabited atoll last week and began an underwater survey of the area of interest.
But the weather - powered by strong El Niño conditions in the Pacific - has so far prevented them from beginning a second of three phases, in which underwater objects will be probed to determine their depth and sediment will be dredged.
"We're working to get everything done today if we can," Bandla said. "The crew's really excited."
Earhart had already successfully flown from California across South America, Africa and Asia in her twin-engine Lockheed Electra when she arrived in Lae, Papua New Guinea on 2 July 1937.
From there, she and her navigator Fred Noonan had planned to travel towards Hawaii and then finally back to California.
But her plane vanished without a trace while trying to reach Howland Island, a remote, uninhabited coral island near Nikumaroro, to refuel.
One theory is that Earhart unintentionally navigated to Nikumaroro, where she ditched her plane and died a castaway.
Images of the so-called Taraia Object - which Purdue University says is visible in photography dating back to 1938 - show what could be the remnants of a small aircraft sitting in shallow waters, though other explorers remain sceptical.
Interest in the expedition prompted New Zealand's Air Force Museum to publish, external previously unseen reconnaissance images of Nikumaroro on Friday.
While the Taraia Object is not obviously visible in any of the black-and-white slides, taken in 1938 from a seaplane, they do show the beached wreck of the SS Norwich City, a British merchant vessel that ran aground on the island during a storm in 1929, killing 11.
Purdue, which with the US-based Archaeological Legacy Institute (ALI) is spearheading the expedition, said the incident demonstrated the risks surrounding the island.
To get into the atoll's lagoon, a boat has to navigate through a narrow gap created in the reef by the British in 1963 - the last time the island was inhabited.
But the university said wind gusts of up to 27 knots (31mph) present around the island until Sunday meant the transport boat could be knocked into the reef by crashing waves.
However, it said the Norwich City wreck may lend credence to the researchers' theory.
Purdue said a 15-year-old in Florida reported hearing Earhart's voice repeating "New York City" over her father's shortwave radio shortly after the aviator vanished. Proponents of the castaway theory argue this may have been a misunderstanding of Earhart giving her location as near the Norwich City.
As a result of the three-day hold, the research team has extended the expedition time to complete its fieldwork and has yet to indicate whether they had found any promising evidence of Earhart's plane.
ALI director Rick Pettigrew said the team was aware of the global interest in the expedition and would share its results "as soon as we are able". Purdue suggested before the poor weather hit that it could identify the Taraia Object in a matter of days.
While researchers have previously found evidence of a human presence on the island around the time of Earhart's disappearance, some skeptics believe the Taraia Object was just a tree that had fallen from the atoll into the lagoon.
Previous attempts to find her Electra have also come up short.
In 2024, a group of researchers said they may have found it lying around 4,877m (16,000ft) below the surface near Howland Island through sonar imaging - but this was later confirmed to be a rock formation.
Similarly, an expedition in 2019 to investigate a photograph of what might have been landing gear protruding from the water near Nikumaroro also failed to find anything.

title: Shabana Mahmood to hold talks with EU over law enforcement cooperation
content_c:
The UK home secretary, Shabana Mahmood, will meet the EU’s home affairs commissioner on Monday for further talks just days after Andy Burnham said he wanted to rejoin European law enforcement databases from which the UK has been locked out of since Brexit.
According to the European Commission, they will discuss “migration, border management, law enforcement cooperation and counter-terrorism”, with the latest Frontex data published on Monday showing a 43% decline in small boats crossing the Channel.
It will be the second time Mahmood has met Magnus Brunner in two months and comes amid an increase in engagement between London and Brussels since Andy Burnham announced he would use an upcoming EU-UK summit to “lay out to the country” what he believes are the “different options for Britain’s long-term relationship” with the EU.
Brunner said “the UK’s contribution is indispensable” to continuing efforts to suppress irregular migration after the EU introduced a suite of new laws aimed at speeding up asylum decisions and deportations.
On the agenda for Monday’s meeting will be talks on the UK rejoining some of the police and security databases it was locked out from after Brexit and rejoining a new database, Eurodac, centring on migration.
Last week Burnham told MPs that “one of the most positive aspects of my meeting with [the European Commission] president [Ursula] von der Leyen in New York, was her openness to the conversation about restoring data sharing on immigration across the UK, across Europe”.
He said it was “control” that the UK “lost” and should get “more attention” in the debate about Brexit. “I will work hard to see if we can get a practical arrangement on that very issue at the summit in November,” Burnham said.
Brunner will also meet the MI5 director general, Ken McCallum, and visit the National Counter Terrorism Security Office, as well as meet senior officials from the UK’s child sexual abuse centre to discuss joint efforts to tackle such crimes.
He has also been chosen to deliver a lecture at King’s College London on migration and asylum, where he will talk about the impact of the EU’s new Pact on Migration and Asylum, a framework of 10 pieces of legislation overhauling how the EU manages its borders, processes asylum applications and shares information among member states.
Brunner will tell those he meets that the new laws have already had a significant impact along with a shift in political priorities around migration in key countries such as Germany, Italy and France.
He said the “reforms are paying” off in the UK too, with illegal crossings down 43%.
“We must stay on this course, including along all relevant migration routes, and the UK’s contribution is indispensable,” he said. “We have put our European house in order. Illegal crossings at our external borders are down 55% over two years, with a further third this year, and asylum applications are at record lows in the countries that used to be main destinations.”
One key database the UK wants access to is Eurodac, a new platform which collects fingerprints and facial images of asylum seekers from the age of six, and security flags for people linked to terrorism or serious crime.
Another is the Schengen Information System (SIS), which contains data on missing persons, stolen goods, vehicles and number plates, and fugitives crossing internal EU borders. About 20m searches are made daily on the SIS, according to EU data, mostly on cars.
The Home Office has not commented.

title: Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
content_c:
Is Germany's eight-hour workday under threat?
October 18, 2026
The town of Leuna, in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt, is one of the country's largest chemical industry hub, where more than 100 companies have established operations. Among them is the Finnish biotechnology group UPM, which has recently built a biorefinery for wood-based chemicals in Leuna. It's now hiring.
One of the job listings is for a chemical technician to oversee the rollout of new facilities. But to qualify, candidates must be willing to work 12-hour shifts. Is that legal? According to German law, standard working hours are limited to eight hours per day. It is permissible to extend this to ten hours, provided that workers receive compensatory time off for the overtime, and there must be at least 11 hours of rest between two shifts.
Twelve-hour shifts? What German law permits
Business associations and the conservative Christian Democratic Union (CDU) and Christian Social Union (CSU) parties have long called for these rules to be made more flexible.
Rainer Dulger, president of the Confederation of German Employers' Associations (BDA), points to the European Working Time Directive, which allows for a maximum weekly working time of 48 hours. "The allowance is being taken advantage of almost everywhere else — except here," Dulger told the dpa news agency in August.
Companies say they often find the existing rules too rigid, particularly in industries with seasonal fluctuations — such as tourism — or in project-based work, or during irregular peaks in workload, such as in the restaurant industry. They could deploy their staff more efficiently, says Dulger: "The Working Hours Act dates back to the era of fax machines and rotary-dial phones. It knows nothing of laptops or daycare hours."
CDU and SPD divided on working hours
In their 2025 coalition agreement, the CDU/CSU and the center-left Social Democratic Party (SPD) agreed to reform the Working Hours Act. "In keeping with the European Working Time Directive, we want to allow for a maximum weekly rather than daily working time — also and especially to promote a better work-life balance," the agreement said.
The SPD would have preferred to leave the law unchanged, but had to accept the conservative parties' plans. The Social Democrats pointed out that longer working hours are already permitted in exceptional cases, such as in emergency services, the health care sector and security services. Workers in power plants, refineries and the chemical industry are also allowed to work up to 12 hours at a time.
A surprise for Chancellor Friedrich Merz
Even Chancellor Friedrich Merz himself seemed unaware of this exception until quite recently. After visiting the UPM refinery in Leuna in September, he recounted to business leaders at the German Employers' Day in Berlin that he was "completely surprised" to learn that the facilities operate on a continuous 12-hour shift schedule, thanks to the approval of the works council.
Merz recounted the shift supervisor describing the work schedule as "really great" — with three-day work weeks. "He said we have plenty of time for our families — it's a great way to organize things." Merz went on to conclude that this demonstrates the benefits of relaxing the Working Hours Act.
"Working more than eight hours is not exploitation. Rather, it can be a good opportunity to organize working hours more flexibly — both for businesses and for the people working there," the chancellor said. "We should do it."
SPD agrees to longer working hours, but with conditions
But there is resistance from within the SPD and from trade unions opposed to amending the Working Hours Act. The trade union Verdi argues that significantly longer workdays would have negative consequences for employees' health and would disadvantage people with family and caregiving responsibilities. In certain industries, employees could also be put under pressure to accept longer shifts.
An initial reform draft was drawn up in June 2026 by the Labor and Social Affairs Ministry, headed at the time by Bärbel Bas, an SPD politician who has since resigned for personal reasons.
The draft includes some conditions, including a collective bargaining agreement between employers and unions if any schedule changes were made, as well as health and safety regulations, and working hours to be tracked electronically.
Dispute over collective bargaining rights and worker protection
Annika Klose, spokesperson for labor and social policy for the SPD parliamentary group, explained the thinking behind the idea. Flexibility, she said, is "not a one-way street." The coalition agreement explicitly aims to promote a better balance between family and work. "So that it's sometimes possible to take your child to football practice in the afternoon and then continue working afterward — but not that my boss tells me against my will: 'You're working the shift from 9 a.m. to 10 p.m. tomorrow.'"
The CDU/CSU immediately rejected the draft. Businesses were also up in arms. "This draft must be withdrawn and completely revised," demanded Dulger in a statement, saying it was "steeped in mistrust." The German Confederation of Skilled Crafts (ZDH) spoke of a "breach of the commitments agreed to in the coalition agreement." The reform has been on hold ever since.
Why the reform stalled
At the Employers' Day event, Merz held out the prospect of progress. "This is indeed long overdue. I believe we can accomplish this relatively quickly and create flexibility in the labor market."
It remains to be seen, however, whether the new SPD Labor Minister, Alexander Schweitzer, shares this view. In early October, his party released a paper on reforming working hours that read like a declaration of war against the CDU. "Self-determination, Not Deregulation" is the title of the seven-page document that was signed by the SPD working group on labor, the youth organization Jusos, the "60plus" working group and the women's wing of the SPD.
In the paper, the Social Democrats not only reiterate the points that already appeared in Bas' draft back in June. They also demand that, in the future, employers and employees should decide on working hours "jointly and by mutual agreement." They argued that it is not "in the spirit of a modern reform of working time law" if only employers can determine when employees finish work.
From a political perspective, the dispute over reforming work hours has long become more than just a debate over legal provisions. It is a fundamental dispute over how much flexibility workers should be expected to tolerate in the future and to what extent the state should protect them. And it is yet another stumbling block for the already beleaguered government in Berlin.
This article was translated from German.

According to German law, standard working hours are limited to eight hours per day. It is permissible to extend this to ten hours, provided that workers receive compensatory time off for the overtime, and there must be at least 11 hours of rest between two shifts.

title: Deutsche Bahn: ICE-Lokführer vergisst, in Fulda anzuhalten
content_c:
Halt verpasst ICE-Lokführer vergisst, in Fulda anzuhalten
Einige Passagiere eines voll besetzten ICE mussten am Sonntag einen ungeplanten Umweg einlegen – offenbar, weil der Lokführer den Stopp in Fulda vergessen hatte. Eine Schaffnerin habe durchgesagt, dass sie es nicht mehr rechtzeitig geschafft habe, den Lokführer zu informieren, dass er hätte halten müssen, berichtete eine dpa-Reporterin, die in dem Zug unterwegs war.
Stattdessen hielt der ICE 596 dann in Hünfeld, einer etwa 18 Kilometer entfernten Kleinstadt in Osthessen. Alle Fahrgäste, die nach Fulda wollten, mussten am Sonntagnachmittag dort aussteigen und mit einem Regionalzug zurückfahren. Weil der Fernzug für den Bahnsteig dort zu lang war, wurden die Türen der Wagen der 1. Klasse in Hünfeld nicht geöffnet.
Ein Sprecher der Deutschen Bahn sagte der Deutschen Presse-Agentur, der Triebfahrzeugführer habe den Halt in Fulda versehentlich vergessen. »Wir bitten alle Fahrgäste ausdrücklich um Entschuldigung.« Die betroffenen Passagiere könnten eine Entschädigung im Rahmen der Fahrgastrechte beantragen, so der Sprecher.
Der Zug sollte planmäßig 16.15 Uhr in Frankfurt starten – und dann über Fulda, Eisenach, Erfurt, Leipzig und Wittenberg nach Berlin fahren. Er startete in Frankfurt allerdings später, weil mehrere Wagen überfüllt waren und das Zugpersonal die Fahrgäste aufforderte, sich in den vorderen Wagen zu verteilen. Erst mit rund 15 Minuten Verspätung ging es dann los.

title: Iran unterbreitet den USA ein Angebot - und droht zugleich
content_c:
Krieg in Nahost Irans neuer Verteidigungsminister droht den USA
Irans Regierung hat gemischte Signale nach Washington gesendet: Während Außenminister Araghtschi das Angebot erneuerte, die Straße von Hormus zu öffnen, drohte der neu ernannte Verteidigungsminister Ketabtschi US-Präsident Trump.
Iran hat sein Angebot an die USA zur Wiedereröffnung der Straße von Hormus untermauert. Die Öffnung der Meerenge könne innerhalb von sieben Tagen stattfinden, sagte Außenminister Abbas Araghtschi am Rande eines Treffens der Organisation für Islamische Zusammenarbeit in Bagdad. Als Bedingungen nannte er erneut ein Ende der US-Blockade iranischer Häfen sowie der Sanktionen gegen Ölexporte.
Nach Angaben Araghtschis prüft die iranische Regierung derzeit ein Angebot der USA. Washington fordert eine deutliche Reduzierung der iranischen Uran-Anreicherung, um den seit acht Monaten andauernden Krieg zu beenden.
Durch die strategisch wichtige Meerenge lief vor dem Krieg etwa ein Fünftel des weltweiten Handels mit Öl und Flüssigerdgas (LNG). Seit der Schließung der Straße von Hormus sind die Energiepreise weltweit auf einem Höhenflug.
Drohung von Irans neuem Verteidigungsminister
Während Außenminister Aragtschi mit einem Angebot an Washington herantrat, formulierte sein neuer Kabinettskollege, der heute vom iranischen Parlament als Verteidigungsminister bestätigte Luftfahrtexperte Mehrdad Achlaghi Ketabtschi, eine Drohnung gegen die USA. Präsident Donald Trump solle sich darauf konzentrieren, seine Truppen sicher aus der Region abzuziehen. Sollte der - so wörtlich - "amerikanische Feind" eine weitere Fehlkalkulation begehen, werde die Antwort "überraschend und umfassend" ausfallen, so Ketabtschi. Damit reagierte er auf Berichte, wonach die USA planen, erneut iranische Atomanlagen anzugreifen.
Die US-Armee "wird es sehr wahrscheinlich nicht wagen, uns erneut anzugreifen", sagte Ketabtschi. "Sollte sie es doch tun, muss sie mit erheblichen Schäden rechnen - genauso wie die ganze Region." Über Trump sagte er: "Wenn er eine einzige Bombe abwirft, muss er sehen, wie viele seiner Soldaten er anschließend in horizontaler Lage aus der Region abtransportieren muss."
Langjähriger Funktionär des Mullah-Regimes
Ketabtschi war bisher Chef der staatlichen Organisation für Luft- und Raumfahrtindustrie und steht auf Sanktionslisten der USA und der EU. Der 68-Jährige erhielt nach Angaben der Regierung 237 Ja-Stimmen im Parlament. Insgesamt wurden demnach 277 Stimmzettel abgegeben. Ketabtschi tritt die Nachfolge von General Asis Nasirsadeh an, der Ende Februar am ersten Tag der Angriffe der USA und Israels getötet worden war.
Seither war das Amt vakant gewesen und wurde kommissarisch von einem General der Revolutionsgarden ausgeübt. Die Elitearmee und der oberste Führer, Modschtaba Chamenei, fällen normalerweise die wichtigsten militärischen Entscheidungen. Ketabtschi hatte 42 Jahre lang für das Ministerium gearbeitet, bekleidet aber keinen militärischen Rang. Seit 2013 stand er an der Spitze eines Verbands der iranischen Rüstungsindustrie.
Mit Informationen von Christian Buttkereit, ARD-Studio Istanbul

title: Курс валют на 19 жовтня: скільки коштують долар, євро і злотий
content_c:
Курс валют на 19 жовтня: скільки коштують долар, євро і злотий
Після вихідних гривня трохи посилилася щодо американського долара.
НБУ встановив офіційний курс валют на понеділок, 19 жовтня. Долар втратив у ціні 2 коп. Євро злетів на 19 коп. Вартість злотого зросла на 4 коп.
Про це йдеться на сайті Національного банку.
Курс долара
- 1 долар США — 44,86 (-2 коп.)
Курс євро
- 1 євро — 50,49 (+19 коп.)
Курс злотого
- 1 польський злотий— 11,55 (+4 коп.)
Нагадаємо, банкір Тарас Лєсовий оцінив, що буде з курсом долара і євро найближчими тижнями. За попереднім прогнозом, різких коливань курсу не буде. Водночас стабільність ринку залежить від втручання Національного банку — обсяги його валютних інтервенцій за останні два місяці зросли на 30–35%.

title: Трамп поддержал Нетаньяху перед парламентскими выборами
content_c:
Президент Соединённых Штатов Дональд Трамп публично поддержал премьер-министра Израиля Биньямина Нетаньяху накануне парламентских выборов. Его заявление может вернуть израильскому политику часть колеблющихся избирателей. Об этом сообщило информационное агентство Reuters.
В воскресенье, 18 октября, Трамп обратился к израильским избирателям. Он назвал Нетаньяху «великим премьером-воином» и партнером в деле достижения мира. Отдельно президент США отметил участие Израиля в совместных американо-израильских ударах по Ирану.
Американский президент высоко оценил стойкость израильского премьера. По его словам, Нетаньяху оставался сильным, смелым и блестящим лидером, несмотря на мощное противодействие, в частности внутри самого Израиля. Трамп подчеркнул, что наблюдал за ним в самые сложные времена. По его мнению, обычные мужчины или женщины под таким давлением могли бы сломаться, однако Нетаньяху выстоял и стал еще сильнее.
Обращаясь к «великому народу Израиля», Трамп заявил о своей полной и безоговорочной поддержке Нетаньяху в его стремлении вновь возглавить правительство. Однако пока неясно, поможет ли этот сигнал самому премьеру и его правой партии «Ликуд». Популярность американского президента среди израильтян снизилась на фоне разногласий между Вашингтоном и Израилем по поводу Ирана. Поэтому публичное одобрение со стороны Трампа не гарантирует дополнительных голосов.
Опросы показывают, что ни у одного из претендентов на данный момент нет очевидного пути к формированию правительства. Должность премьер-министра в Израиле получают благодаря созданию парламентской коалиции. Прямого всенародного голосования за главу правительства нет.
Предстоящие выборы определят, сохранит ли Нетаньяху власть после одного из важнейших периодов в истории страны или уступит центристским соперникам, обещающим начало новой эпохи. Это будет первое общенациональное голосование после нападения ХАМАС 7 октября 2023 года.
Нетаньяху оперативно отреагировал на обращение Трампа: в соцсети X он поблагодарил своего «дорогого друга Дональда» и написал: «Вместе мы завершим миссию!»
Старший научный сотрудник внепартийного Израильского института демократии в Иерусалиме Тамар Герман считает, что запоздалая поддержка Трампа может вернуть Нетаньяху часть сторонников, которые начали сомневаться в своём выборе. Однако широкого притока новых голосов она не ожидает. В отличие от американцев, большинство израильтян в целом поддерживали войну с Ираном. Это касается даже многих критиков Нетаньяху и его правительства.
Аналитик Фонда Карнеги за международный мир в Вашингтоне Аарон Дэвид Миллер отметил, что при столь близких результатах поддержка Трампа «не может ему навредить и может помочь». В то же время опросы прогнозируют потерю парламентского большинства религиозно-националистической коалицией Нетаньяху. У оппозиции также может не хватить возможностей для формирования правительства. При таком сценарии Нетаньяху может остаться исполняющим обязанности премьера до проведения следующих выборов.
По мнению Миллера, Трамп ранее не воспользовался возможностями поддержать израильского премьера, возможно, потому что стремился сохранить рычаги влияния на него в вопросах Газы или Ливана. В итоге американский президент встал на сторону политика, которого считает сильным и несправедливо преследуемым.
«Как бы ни был разгневан Трамп на Нетаньяху за развязывание этой войны с Ираном, в конечном итоге это было решение Трампа», — добавил Миллер.
Он добавил, что отказ поддержать Нетаньяху мог бы вызвать обоснованные вопросы к самому Трампу. В частности, стоило ли ему вообще начинать всю иранскую кампанию.
Напомним, что администрация Дональда Трампа подготовила масштабные ограничения в отношении Международного уголовного суда после выдачи ордера на арест Биньямина Нетаньяху. МУС также выдал ордер в отношении бывшего министра обороны Израиля Йоава Галланта по делу о предполагаемых военных преступлениях в Газе. Оба политика отвергают обвинения.
Кроме того, накануне выборов Нетаньяху оказался под давлением из-за утверждений о предупреждении перед нападением ХАМАС 7 октября 2023 года. Президент ОАЭ Мохаммед бин Заид якобы сообщил ему о подготовке крупной атаки примерно за десять дней до нападения. Согласно этим утверждениям, премьер не передал информацию руководителям силовых структур.
description: Опросы не гарантируют большинства ни одному из лагерей, а война с Ираном разделяет избирателей обеих стран.
content:
Президент Соединённых Штатов Дональд Трамп публично поддержал премьер-министра Израиля Биньямина Нетаньяху накануне парламентских выборов. Его заявление может вернуть израильскому политику часть колеблющихся избирателей. Об этом сообщило информационное агентство Reuters.

Американский президент высоко оценил стойкость израильского премьера. По его словам, Нетаньяху оставался сильным, смелым и блестящим лидером, несмотря на мощное противодействие, в частности внутри самого Израиля. Трамп подчеркнул, что наблюдал за ним в самые сложные времена. По его мнению, обычные мужчины или женщины под таким давлением могли бы сломаться, однако Нетаньяху выстоял и стал еще сильнее.
Обращаясь к «великому народу Израиля», Трамп заявил о своей полной и безоговорочной поддержке Нетаньяху в его стремлении вновь возглавить правительство. Однако пока неясно, поможет ли этот сигнал самому премьеру и его правой партии «Ликуд». Популярность американского президента среди израильтян снизилась на фоне разногласий между Вашингтоном и Израилем по поводу Ирана. Поэтому публичное одобрение со стороны Трампа не гарантирует дополнительных голосов.
Опросы показывают, что ни у одного из претендентов на данный момент нет очевидного пути к формированию правительства. Должность премьер-министра в Израиле получают благодаря созданию парламентской коалиции. Прямого всенародного голосования за главу правительства нет.
Предстоящие выборы определят, сохранит ли Нетаньяху власть после одного из важнейших периодов в истории страны или уступит центристским соперникам, обещающим начало новой эпохи. Это будет первое общенациональное голосование после нападения ХАМАС 7 октября 2023 года.
Нетаньяху оперативно отреагировал на обращение Трампа: в соцсети X он поблагодарил своего «дорогого друга Дональда» и написал: «Вместе мы завершим миссию!»
Старший научный сотрудник внепартийного Израильского института демократии в Иерусалиме Тамар Герман считает, что запоздалая поддержка Трампа может вернуть Нетаньяху часть сторонников, которые начали сомневаться в своём выборе. Это касается даже многих критиков Нетаньяху и его правительства.
Аналитик Фонда Карнеги за международный мир в Вашингтоне Аарон Дэвид Миллер отметил, что при столь близких результатах поддержка Трампа «не может ему навредить и может помочь». title: Росіяни вдарили по приватним будинкам в Дніпрі, під завалами можуть бути люди – ОВА
content_c:
Російські окупанти в ніч на понеділок, 19 жовтня, завдали удару по Дніпру, повідомляє очільник Дніпропетровської обласної військової адміністрації Олександр Ганжа.
"Пошкоджені приватні будинки. За попередньою інформацією, у них можуть бути заблоковані люди", – написав Ганжа в телеграм-каналі.
Наразі на місці працюють усі служби.

title: European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
content_c:
European diplomats attacked by Israeli settlers in West Bank
- Published
A delegation of European diplomats has been attacked by masked Israeli settlers in the occupied West Bank.
Belgium condemned the assault on its consul general and the other envoys, while France decried the attack as "appalling". Both called for Israel to bring those responsible to justice.
The Israel Defense Forces (IDF) also condemned what they called "the severe act of violence" and said they were investigating.
But the office of the Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu cast doubt on what happened, suggesting it was part of a "co-ordinated campaign to smear Israel".
The attack came only a day after a number of Palestinians and Heidi Levine, a Washington Post photographer, were injured in a separate assault by settlers in another village in the West Bank.
US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said the attack on Levine was "disturbing" and "not a good look".
It was also condemned by the US ambassador to Israel, Mike Huckabee, who called it a "despicable act of terror carried out by masked cowards". A staunch ally of Israel, Huckabee said the assailants must face "prosecution to the fullest extent of the law".
In Saturday's incident, the European diplomats - from Belgium, France, Poland and the Catholic Church - had come to the largely Christian village of Taybeh near Ramallah.
They were there to assess the situation on the ground after almost near daily attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians trying to bring in their olive harvest.
Video footage from the scene showed masked settlers confronting the convoy. Reports suggest stones were thrown.
The Belgian authorities said a car from its consulate had a window smashed and a French mayor was assaulted. Video showed a man wearing a French tricolor sash slumped beside a vehicle.
Belgium's foreign minister Maxime Prevot condemned the attack and said Israel had a responsibility to bring those responsible to justice, as well as ensuring the safety of diplomats, journalists and Palestinians.
"Palestinians face this violence every day. Settlers also target journalists reporting on it and diplomats. Harvesting olives, reporting the news or carrying out diplomatic duties should never put anyone at risk of attack," he said.
He also said Belgium will continue to press for EU sanctions against those responsible for the violence.
France's Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot echoed those sentiments, calling on Israeli authorities to "urgently halt this criminal violence and guarantee the safety of civilian populations".
Poland's foreign affairs ministry also called for a "firm response" from Israeli authorities and for "an end to the spiral of violence in the West Bank".
The EU condemned the attacks, urged Israel to abide by international and human rights law, and end the expansion of settlements.
A spokesperson said that while they acknowledged some Israeli officials had condemned the attacks, they said they still expect "full accountability as well as effective measures" to stop the continued violence against Palestinians and journalists.
Gideon Sa'ar, Israel's foreign minister, said he strongly condemned the violence by what he called "Israeli rioters". He said the foreign ministry was in contact with the ambassadors of the countries involved.
But he added: "Without detracting from the severity of the incident, it is unfortunate that the visit was not coordinated with the IDF in advance. Such coordination could have helped safeguard the visitors' security."
The IDF said they "strongly condemn the severe act of violence that took place in the area of Taybeh, during which diplomatic representatives were attacked by Israeli rioters."
"According to a preliminary inquiry, no IDF soldiers were present at the scene at the time of the attack," they added.
But Netanyahu's office urged "caution before drawing conclusions" from reports about the attack.
It said the images on social media "do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility".
A statement continued: "Those circumstances remain under investigation. Israeli police and forensic investigators have launched an investigation to establish the facts and identify those responsible."
It added that "these reports come amid concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel and the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria during the annual olive harvest, relying on sensational headlines before the full facts emerge".
Netanyahu's office named the injured French official as Bernard Baudoux. The left-wing mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France told the AFP news agency the attack showed a tolerance by Israel's right-wing government for settler violence.
The mayor said the settlers kicked him and beat him with iron bars, throwing him to the ground.
"It's the gratuitous nature of the violence that stuns me," he said. "They arrived completely enraged."
"The whole world needs to know what's happening there. For me, I'll go back to my country and everything will be fine. Those who continue to suffer the most are those who are here," he said.

title: Zelenskyy thanks Trump for resumed intelligence sharing after US Starlink ‘message’
content_c:
Volodymyr Zelenskyy on Sunday thanked the Trump administration for resuming intelligence sharing between the two countries, but maintained the US had intentionally throttled its Starlink satellite internet access so that Donald Trump could send a “message” in his ongoing feud with the Ukrainian president.
In an interview on NBC, Zelenskyy said the US had “unblocked” intelligence on impending Russian ballistic missile strikes, which have pounded the country’s energy infrastructure as winter draws in.
“It was blocked for some period of time. And then it was deblocked by the American side. We are very thankful for this. Now it works,” Zelenskyy told NBC’s Meet the Press. “Only [the] United States has this unique intelligence to tell our side when Russia uses ballistic missiles. And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days.”
Zelenskyy also said that Elon Musk’s SpaceX was responsible for suddenly limiting the speed at which Starlink terminals worked in Ukraine, hampering drone operations on the frontlines as well as some air defence missions.
“It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed,” he said. “And technically, SpaceX did it.”
Two people were killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continued to trade strikes on each other’s power infrastructure, after the breakdown of Trump’s short-lived and unilaterally declared “energy ceasefire”.
Trump has increasingly sought a detente with Moscow, inking a deal to import diesel fuel from Russia and waiving sanctions voted for overwhelmingly by both houses of Congress. Zelenskyy has become increasingly critical of Trump’s actions as the US has piled pressure on Ukraine to cease striking refineries in Russia and end the war quickly on Putin’s terms.
“We want to trust him and I hope that he will change his decisions,” Zelenskyy said of Trump. “Because I think that it’s all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help [the] United States.”
Zelenskyy on Sunday said that he had spoken with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the two Trump envoys charged with ending the war in Ukraine, as part of Ukraine’s “virtually nonstop communication” with the Trump administration.
But the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, in a separate interview on NBC on Sunday said that Zelenskyy had been “reckless” to accuse the Trump administration of standing behind the throttling of Starlink.
“President Trump and Secretary Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that,” said Bessent. “And I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge.”
He added: “President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren’t true.”
On Sunday night Trump said Zelenskyy did not want his nation’s more than four-year war with Russia to end, writing on his Truth Social platform that he was in the process of negotiating a peace between Russia and Ukraine and making “great progress” but claimed: “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.”
Ukraine has resumed striking refineries in Russia and on Sunday attacked one of the country’s main oil terminals.
One person was killed and 15 wounded overnight after Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.
St Petersburg’s governor, Alexander Beglov, said on Sunday that fires had broken out overnight at the city’s oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses. A logistics centre belonging to the Russian retailer Ozon and a datacentre for the local tech company VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.
Alexander Drozdenko, the governor of the Leningrad region that surrounds St Petersburg, said 145 drones had been shot down and about 20,000 people were without electricity after the raid. “A large-scale [unmanned aerial vehicle] attack continues to be repelled,” he wrote on Telegram.
Fears that the conflict could be spilling over into Nato’s borders were stoked again on Sunday morning after Lithuania told residents in central and northern parts of the country to seek shelter for about an hour after an unidentified flying object entered its airspace.
During the red alert, Nato fighter jets were scrambled to the area and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania’s second largest city, was temporarily closed, the national crisis management centre said.
The Nato aircraft were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy weather and did not attempt to shoot it down, the centre said.
Ukraine’s foreign ministry later said it regretted the possible diversion of its drones into Lithuanian airspace on Sunday, which it said may have been caused by Russian electronic warfare.
“We apologise for any disruption, risks and concern this may have caused,” a spokesperson, Heorhii Tykhyi, wrote on X. “We are committed to sharing all relevant information with our Lithuanian partners to establish the full circumstances of the incident.”
Meanwhile, local officials in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia said Russian strikes had killed a woman and wounded at least two other people, including a six-year-old girl. Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution had been damaged by the attack, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia regional military administration.
Tensions are deepening between Kyiv and Washington, with the US president criticising Ukraine for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, despite continued Russian aggression.
Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” last week – which neither side said they agreed to beforehand – that quickly collapsed as Moscow continued its strikes on Ukraine’s power grid and Kyiv eventually resumed its hits on Russian oil refineries.
The Russian defence ministry said its air defence units had downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones around the country overnight. The Tass news agency quoted the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, who said Russia was responding with systematic, large-scale strikes.
“The Kyiv regime is resisting, but this cannot change the course of events,” he said, answering a question about how Russia might respond to Kyiv’s attack on St Petersburg.
On Saturday, Russia said it had carried out a major overnight attack, targeting Ukraine’s largest steelworks in the city of Kryvyi Rih and vessels using the port of Odesa. In a statement, Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had also hit an electricity substation in the north-western city of Zhytomyr and another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia.
In the Trump administration’s latest effort to reduce tensions with Russia, the US president announced on Friday that he would put a hold on a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause on the legislation passed by both chambers was in the national interest.
Trump has yet to give details about what he has decided regarding further sanctions on Russia.
“We’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out,” he told reporters at a fundraising dinner at his Florida estate on Saturday. “But it’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world.”
In a post on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said in the week since Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times.
He also said that the previous night alone, energy facilities in four Ukrainian regions had been attacked and tens of thousands of families were still without power. He accused Russia of trying to cause a blackout.
“America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements,” he said. “On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting.”
Zelenskyy also stressed that the war was continuing due to Russia’s invasion – not because Ukraine was defending itself. “It is Russia that must face pressure for peace to have a chance. Thank you to everyone who understands this and helps,” he said.
Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered Nato airspace in the Baltic region in recent months. Kyiv has said they were steered off course by Russian signal jamming. Such incidents have stoked concerns that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spread.
Reuters, the Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

And we didn’t get it during ballistic attacks during three days.”
Zelenskyy also said that Elon Musk’s SpaceX was responsible for suddenly limiting the speed at which Starlink terminals worked in Ukraine, hampering drone operations on the frontlines as well as some air defence missions.
“It was a message from [the] American government to limit the speed,” he said. “And technically, SpaceX did it.”
Two people were killed and at least 17 injured as Russia and Ukraine continued to trade strikes on each other’s power infrastructure, after the breakdown of Trump’s short-lived and unilaterally declared “energy ceasefire”.
Trump has increasingly sought a detente with Moscow, inking a deal to import diesel fuel from Russia and waiving sanctions voted for overwhelmingly by both houses of Congress. Zelenskyy has become increasingly critical of Trump’s actions as the US has piled pressure on Ukraine to cease striking refineries in Russia and end the war quickly on Putin’s terms.
“We want to trust him and I hope that he will change his decisions,” Zelenskyy said of Trump. “Because I think that it’s all mistakes and it will not help us. And it will not help [the] United States.”
Zelenskyy on Sunday said that he had spoken with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, the two Trump envoys charged with ending the war in Ukraine, as part of Ukraine’s “virtually nonstop communication” with the Trump administration.
But the US treasury secretary, Scott Bessent, in a separate interview on NBC on Sunday said that Zelenskyy had been “reckless” to accuse the Trump administration of standing behind the throttling of Starlink.
“President Trump and Secretary Rubio have categorically said that no one in the Trump administration did that,” said Bessent. “And I think it is very reckless for President Zelenskyy to make such a charge.”
He added: “President Zelenskyy should be very careful about making statements like this that aren’t true.”
On Sunday night Trump said Zelenskyy did not want his nation’s more than four-year war with Russia to end, writing on his Truth Social platform that he was in the process of negotiating a peace between Russia and Ukraine and making “great progress” but claimed: “Zelenskyy doesn’t care, and frankly, with all of the money that Europe is famously giving him … he doesn’t want to end this war, and probably never did.”
Ukraine has resumed striking refineries in Russia and on Sunday attacked one of the country’s main oil terminals.
One person was killed and 15 wounded overnight after Ukraine used more than 1,000 drones to target Russian oil depots, logistics facilities and datacentres in one of its largest ever aerial bombardments.
St Petersburg’s governor, Alexander Beglov, said on Sunday that fires had broken out overnight at the city’s oil terminal, an oil depot and industrial warehouses. A logistics centre belonging to the Russian retailer Ozon and a datacentre for the local tech company VK were also targeted, both companies confirmed.
Alexander Drozdenko, the governor of the Leningrad region that surrounds St Petersburg, said 145 drones had been shot down and about 20,000 people were without electricity after the raid. “A large-scale [unmanned aerial vehicle] attack continues to be repelled,” he wrote on Telegram.
Fears that the conflict could be spilling over into Nato’s borders were stoked again on Sunday morning after Lithuania told residents in central and northern parts of the country to seek shelter for about an hour after an unidentified flying object entered its airspace.
During the red alert, Nato fighter jets were scrambled to the area and Kaunas airport, near Lithuania’s second largest city, was temporarily closed, the national crisis management centre said.
The Nato aircraft were unable to visually identify the object due to cloudy weather and did not attempt to shoot it down, the centre said.
Ukraine’s foreign ministry later said it regretted the possible diversion of its drones into Lithuanian airspace on Sunday, which it said may have been caused by Russian electronic warfare.
“We apologise for any disruption, risks and concern this may have caused,” a spokesperson, Heorhii Tykhyi, wrote on X. “We are committed to sharing all relevant information with our Lithuanian partners to establish the full circumstances of the incident.”
Meanwhile, local officials in the southern Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia said Russian strikes had killed a woman and wounded at least two other people, including a six-year-old girl. Two apartment buildings, 18 cars and an educational institution had been damaged by the attack, according to Mykhailo Semikin, the head of the Zaporizhzhia regional military administration.
Tensions are deepening between Kyiv and Washington, with the US president criticising Ukraine for its strikes on Russian oil infrastructure, despite continued Russian aggression.
Trump announced an “energy ceasefire” last week – which neither side said they agreed to beforehand – that quickly collapsed as Moscow continued its strikes on Ukraine’s power grid and Kyiv eventually resumed its hits on Russian oil refineries.
The Russian defence ministry said its air defence units had downed 1,015 Ukrainian drones around the country overnight. The Tass news agency quoted the Kremlin spokesperson, Dmitry Peskov, who said Russia was responding with systematic, large-scale strikes.
“The Kyiv regime is resisting, but this cannot change the course of events,” he said, answering a question about how Russia might respond to Kyiv’s attack on St Petersburg.
On Saturday, Russia said it had carried out a major overnight attack, targeting Ukraine’s largest steelworks in the city of Kryvyi Rih and vessels using the port of Odesa. In a statement, Russia’s defence ministry said its forces had also hit an electricity substation in the north-western city of Zhytomyr and another steel plant in Zaporizhzhia.
In the Trump administration’s latest effort to reduce tensions with Russia, the US president announced on Friday that he would put a hold on a sweeping new sanctions package targeting the Russian economy, telling Congress the pause on the legislation passed by both chambers was in the national interest.
Trump has yet to give details about what he has decided regarding further sanctions on Russia.
“We’ll figure it out, and you’ll figure it out,” he told reporters at a fundraising dinner at his Florida estate on Saturday. “But it’s a very good decision, and it’s going to be a decision that’s good for the country, and I think good for the world.”
In a post on X on Sunday, Zelenskyy said in the week since Trump’s announcement of an energy ceasefire Russia had attacked Ukraine’s energy, oil and gas sectors 76 times.
He also said that the previous night alone, energy facilities in four Ukrainian regions had been attacked and tens of thousands of families were still without power. He accused Russia of trying to cause a blackout.
“America should see that Russia is not taking any reciprocal steps in response to sanctions relief or agreements,” he said. “On the contrary, they take every signal of an opportunity to make money as proof that their bet on war is paying off and they can keep fighting.”
Zelenskyy also stressed that the war was continuing due to Russia’s invasion – not because Ukraine was defending itself. “It is Russia that must face pressure for peace to have a chance. Thank you to everyone who understands this and helps,” he said.
Ukrainian drones have repeatedly entered Nato airspace in the Baltic region in recent months. Kyiv has said they were steered off course by Russian signal jamming. Such incidents have stoked concerns that Russia’s war in Ukraine could spread.
Reuters, the Associated Press and Agence France-Presse contributed to this report

title: France reports almost 2,400 arrests after riots, looting and arson during cost-of-living protests
content_c:
France: Some 2,400 arrested after looting, arson during protests
October 18, 2026
Almost 2,400 people were arrested across France following riots, looting and arson during cost-of-living protests, France's authorities said.
The unrest on Saturday has sharpened tensions ahead of France's 2027 presidential election, as anger over living costs collides with tight limits on government spending.
What happened during the protests?
Clashes, fires and looting broke out in several cities during Saturday's demonstrations. The country's Interior Ministry said about 1,000 officers were injured.
Paris police reported 855 arrests, describing the figure as a record. Prosecutors said 517 people remained in custody, including 171 minors. Those figures were provisional, with arrests continuing until early Sunday.
Most arrests in the capital were linked to suspected handling of stolen goods, participation in a group intending to commit violence, and vandalism.
In central France, rioters set fire to Limoges' historic town hall, leaving much of it gutted. Mayor Guillaume Guerin condemned the destruction.
"There are no words to condemn what happened, so appalling is it," he told broadcaster LCI. "The country is in chaos."
Authorities reported attacks on public buildings and shops in Marseille, Lyon, Avignon and Grenoble. Police used tear gas, batons and water cannon in several cities.
Demonstrators were also reported injured. The newspaper Le Figaro reported that a 17-year-old lost a hand to a grenade fired by police in Saint-Etienne.
What have leading French politicians said?
President Emmanuel Macron addressed the nation due to the protests, saying "nothing justifies" the violence.
"Tonight, we feel anger and shame," Macron said in a speech, adding that there needs to be a separation between protesters with what he called "legitimate demands" and people who "destroyed, smashed and looted."
The France leader also promised "full transparency" on police's response to the protests.
Opposition politicians seeking to succeed Macron in presidential elections in April and May also responded to the unrest.
Far-right candidate Marine Le Pen accused the party of her far-left rival Jean-Luc Melenchon of having "legitimized the violence." She pledged to protect the French "from the violence of the extreme left."
Melenchon, who had backed the demonstrations and preceding student protests, urged demonstrators to stay away from looting, calling it "contrary to our methods."
The demonstrations brought together grievances over fuel prices, low wages and problems facing farmers and firefighters. School and university students demanding better learning conditions also participated.
The interior ministry put nationwide turnout at 550,000, including 110,000 in Paris. The CGT trade union gave a higher national estimate of 800,000.
France's high debt and budget deficit limit the government's ability to meet demands for additional spending.
Online calls to revive the yellow vest movement have added to government concerns that student demonstrations could grow into broader unrest.
The yellow vest movement began in 2018 over planned fuel tax increases and grew into wider protests over living costs and inequality. Named after the high-visibility vests worn by demonstrators, it brought months of nationwide demonstrations, some marked by violent clashes with police.
Edited by: Karl Sexton, Jenipher Camino Gonzalez

title: Fake-Sneaker sind ein riesiges Geschäft - doch Käufer gehen in Risiko
content_c:
Gefälschte Markenschuhe Fake-Sneaker - ein riesiges und riskantes Geschäft
Sneaker-Kultmodelle können vierstellige Summen kosten. Viele Menschen greifen daher zu deutlich günstigeren Kopien. Doch das kann gefährlich werden.
Teures Original oder günstiges Replikat? Für Christopher Blumenthal ist diese Frage eigentlich ziemlich leicht zu beantworten. Der Sneaker-Fan hat 2013 "Dead Stock" gegründet, einen Sneakerblog, mit dem er seine Leidenschaft zum Beruf gemacht hat. Doch auch er hat schon gefälschte Sneaker gekauft: "Ich erinnere mich an eine Situation, da habe ich einen Asics aus meiner Sammlung getauscht gegen einen Yeezy 700." Ohne den Schuh richtig anzuschauen, habe er ihn einfach zu seiner Sammlung gepackt. "Dann stellte sich heraus: Das war tatsächlich eine Fälschung."
Dass ihm nicht sofort auffiel, dass es sich beim Schuh um einen Fake handelt, liegt vor allem daran, dass diese nachgemachten Modelle immer besser werden, wie er in der aktuellen Folge des ARD-Formats ECHT? erzählt: "Ich würde behaupten, dass der Fake-Markt mittlerweile so professionell ist, dass auch geübte Sammler teilweise nicht mehr richtig erkennen, ob der Schuh echt ist oder Fake."
40 Euro statt 1.000 Euro?
Und genau das macht die Fälschungen so attraktiv. Wenn nicht mehr auffällt, ob der Chanel-Sneaker 40 Euro gekostet hat oder im Original eine vierstellige Summe, dann greifen immer mehr Menschen zu Fälschungen. Studien zeigen, dass Fake-Shopping längst kein Randphänomen mehr ist: Schon 2023 gaben in einer Umfrage des europäischen Amts für geistiges Eigentum (EUIPO) 34 Prozent der Befragten an, wissentlich ein gefälschtes Produkt gekauft zu haben.
Vor allem Social Media befeuert den Hype um gefakte Markenprodukte zusätzlich. Auf TikTok und in Telegram-Gruppen ist ein ganz eigener Markt dafür entstanden. Mitglieder geben sich dort gegenseitig Tipps zu den neusten Fake-Hypes. Die ECHT-Redaktion wurde für die Recherche selbst Mitglied in einer solchen Telegram-Gruppe mit über 30.000 Mitgliedern. Hier werden täglich Links zu angesagten Fake-Sneakern geteilt.
Die führen etwa zur Marketplace-App "Hacoo", auf der zahlreiche, vor allem chinesische Händler replizierte Luxusprodukte anbieten. Wer die App installiert, kann mit wenigen Klicks Modelle von Prada, Louis Vuitton, Dior oder limitierte Nike-Sneaker bestellen - oft für gerade einmal 40 Euro inklusive Versand, während das Original auf Resale-Märkten locker 1.000 Euro kostet.
Influencer werben aktiv für Fälschungen
Neben solchen Gruppen machen auch viele Influencer und Content-Creator gezielt Werbung für Fake-Ware. Sie stellen sogenannte Spreadsheets vor: Das sind öffentlich einsehbare Tabellen, die wie Verkaufskataloge aufgebaut sind, erklärt der Sneaker-Experte Blumenthal. Dort können Käufer direkt Sneaker, Designeruhren oder Kleidung auswählen und werden zum jeweiligen Hersteller oder Agenten weitergeleitet.
Auf Plattformen wie OOPBUY, SUPERBUY oder ACBUY lassen sich über solche Spreadsheets Repliken bestellen. Da viele dieser Plattformen nicht direkt nach Europa liefern, übernehmen die Shopping-Agenten die Rolle des Zwischenhändlers. Angeboten werden auch sehr rare Modelle wie der Jordan 4 "OFF WHITE" oder der "Union - Guava Ice" als Fakes - für weniger als 100 Dollar, während Originale im Netz mit teils mehr als 6.000 Euro gehandelt werden.
"Schädigen den Ruf unserer Marke"
Auf Anfrage der ECHT-Redaktion zum Umgang damit äußert sich Nike nicht. Adidas schreibt in einer Stellungnahme: "Adidas schützt und verteidigt seine Markenrechte rigoros; dabei gehen wir schwerpunktmäßig gegen Händler und Importeure gefälschter Produkte als auch gegen sogenannte Fakeshops vor."
Dafür arbeite man auch eng mit zuständigen Behörden zusammen, da Fälschungen "aus minderwertigen oder sogar gesundheitsgefährdenden Materialien bestehen" könnten. "Sie schädigen den Ruf unserer Marke, unserer Partner und unserer Beschäftigten, die unermüdlich an der Erforschung und Entwicklung technischer Innovationen und kreativer Designs arbeiten."
Besitz ist in Deutschland nicht strafbar
Wer solche Produkte kauft, bewegt sich rein rechtlich in Deutschland in einer Grauzone: Für den privaten Gebrauch ist Besitz und Kauf in der Regel nicht strafbar. Problematisch wird es beim Handel: Dabei drohen Beschlagnahmung, Vernichtung der Ware und zivilrechtliche Schritte durch Markeninhaber wie beispielsweise Nike oder Adidas.
Praktisch dürften "Fake-Käufer" - rein statistisch gesehen - nicht viel zu befürchten haben. Rund 5,9 Milliarden Pakete mit geringem Warenwert kamen 2025 in der Europäischen Union an, das sind rund 16 Millionen Warensendungen pro Tag. Angesichts dieser Zahlen wird klar, dass nur wenige Sendungen tatsächlich durch den Zoll kontrolliert werden.
"Türkisches Original"
Neben China ist die Türkei ein wichtiger Hotspot für die Produktion von nachgemachten Markenprodukten. Rund zwölf Prozent aller Plagiate kommen aus der Türkei. In Istanbul, einer der größten Textilmetropolen Europas, reicht denn auch ein Blick in die Schaufenster voll günstiger Sneaker oft aus, um Fake Sneaker zu finden. Verkäufer sprechen vom "türkischen Original".
Emre ist einer dieser Basarverkäufer. Er erzählt, dass sie hier durchaus auch Besuch von Markenanwälten und der Polizei bekommen: "Die Anwälte der Markenhersteller kommen und checken, was verkauft wird. Wenn sie was finden, nehmen sie es mit und rufen die Polizei."
Billige Shoppingtour in Istanbul?
Fakes sind allgegenwärtig in der Türkei, denn sie werden auch vor Ort produziert, wie etwa in einer Fabrik außerhalb Istanbuls. Dort riecht es intensiv nach Kleber, überall stehen Kartons, Türen und Gitter, die Atmosphäre ist gedrückt. Eine Produzentin gibt offen zu: "Der weiße Turnschuh ist ein Fake. Ich habe den produziert." Auf die Frage, warum ihre Ware so günstig ist, antwortet sie: "Es ist nur ein kleiner Material- und Qualitätsunterschied. Die Klebestellen halten genauso lange wie beim Original."
Am Ende kostet dieser Schuh auf dem Basar in der türkischen Hauptstadt 16 Euro. Deshalb nutzen viele Urlauber eine Reise in die Türkei auch zum Shoppen. Wer aus dem Urlaub Fakes für den Privatgebrauch mitbringt, der muss in Deutschland in der Regel keine Strafe fürchten.
Außer, dass sie beschlagnahmt werden können. 2024 hat der deutsche Zoll über fünf Millionen Fakes im Wert von 417 Millionen Euro einbehalten. Und in einigen Ländern kann der Kauf von Fakes teuer werden - in Italien sind sogar bis zu 7.000 Euro Strafe möglich.
Schuhe von schlechter Qualität
Und nicht nur finanziell kann der Kauf von Fälschungen ein Risiko sein, auch gesundheitlich. ECHT? hat für die Recherche einige nachgemachte Sneaker gekauft und sie im Prüf- und Forschungsinstitut PFI in Pirmasens untersuchen lassen. Das Institut gilt als eine der etabliertesten Prüfstellen der Schuhbranche.
Die Ergebnisse sind ernüchternd: Der Fake-Adidas "Campus" zeigt zu hohen Abrieb, das Material bildet Löcher, auch im nassen Zustand, und starke Knotenbildung, so Diplom-Ingenieur Kai Tinschert, der die Tests durchgeführt hat. Auch die anderen Fake-Sneaker fallen im Test durch. Beim Nike-Fake "Air Force CPFM" bricht die Laufsohle im Test vollständig - "katastrophal" lautet das Urteil.
Gefährliche Schadstoffe in Fakes
Noch brisanter sind die Ergebnisse der Schadstoffanalyse. In einem Nike-Fake wird ein Lösemittel gefunden, Dimethylformamid, das häufig zur Herstellung synthetischer Materialien verwendet wird. "Dimethylformamid ist ein starkes Gift. Es führt zu Reizungen und ist lebertoxisch", erklärt die Chemie-Expertin Ines Anderie.
Das Problem daran ist: Solche Stoffe gasen aus den Schuhen aus, "selbst wenn man die auf die Terrasse stellt und länger auslüften lässt", so Anderie. "Wenn man die wieder reinholt ins Zimmer, dann wird das immer weiter ausgasen." Betroffen sind aber nicht nur Käufer, sondern vor allem die Beschäftigten in den Fabriken, die täglich mit diesen Chemikalien arbeiten.
Auch im Fake-Adidas "Samba" werden Schadstoffe gefunden, konkret ein verbotener Weichmacher: DEHP. Der Grenzwert ist überschritten, der Schuh dürfte in Deutschland gar nicht verkauft werden. Expertin Anderie erklärt: "Diese Substanzen haben hormonaktive Wirkung. Sie können die Fortpflanzung beeinträchtigen, das Kind im Mutterleib schädigen und im schlimmsten Fall Krebs auslösen." Die vermeintlichen Schnäppchen können also mit erheblichen Gesundheitsrisiken belastet sein.
Gefälschte Waren erkennen
Um Käufer davor zu schützen, dass sie wie Christopher Blumenthal versehentlich gefälschte Waren kaufen, bieten Dienste wie "LegitGrails" eine Authentifizierung per App an. Nutzer laden Detailfotos ihrer Schuhe hoch, die von geschulten Experten und unterstützender KI geprüft werden.
Das Unternehmen wirbt mit einer Genauigkeit von 99,89 Prozent. Auch die vier im Labor untersuchten Fälschungen hat die App innerhalb von 30 Minuten klar als Fälschungen erkannt - trotz ihres hochwertigen Aussehens.

Teures Original oder günstiges Replikat? Für Christopher Blumenthal ist diese Frage eigentlich ziemlich leicht zu beantworten. Der Sneaker-Fan hat 2013 "Dead Stock" gegründet, einen Sneakerblog, mit dem er seine Leidenschaft zum Beruf gemacht hat. Doch auch er hat schon gefälschte Sneaker gekauft: "Ich erinnere mich an eine Situation, da habe ich einen Asics aus meiner Sammlung getauscht gegen einen Yeezy 700." Ohne den Schuh richtig anzuschauen, habe er ihn einfach zu seiner Sammlung gepackt. "Dann stellte sich heraus: Das war tatsächlich eine Fälschung."
Dass ihm nicht sofort auffiel, dass es sich beim Schuh um einen Fake handelt, liegt vor allem daran, dass diese nachgemachten Modelle immer besser werden, wie er in der aktuellen Folge des ARD-Formats ECHT? erzählt: "Ich würde behaupten, dass der Fake-Markt mittlerweile so professionell ist, dass auch geübte Sammler teilweise nicht mehr richtig erkennen, ob der Schuh echt ist oder Fake."
40 Euro statt 1.000 Euro?
Und genau das macht die Fälschungen so attraktiv. Wenn nicht mehr auffällt, ob der Chanel-Sneaker 40 Euro gekostet hat oder im Original eine vierstellige Summe, dann greifen immer mehr Menschen zu Fälschungen. Studien zeigen, dass Fake-Shopping längst kein Randphänomen mehr ist: Schon 2023 gaben in einer Umfrage des europäischen Amts für geistiges Eigentum (EUIPO) 34 Prozent der Befragten an, wissentlich ein gefälschtes Produkt gekauft zu haben.
Vor allem Social Media befeuert den Hype um gefakte Markenprodukte zusätzlich. Auf TikTok und in Telegram-Gruppen ist ein ganz eigener Markt dafür entstanden. Mitglieder geben sich dort gegenseitig Tipps zu den neusten Fake-Hypes. Die ECHT-Redaktion wurde für die Recherche selbst Mitglied in einer solchen Telegram-Gruppe mit über 30.000 Mitgliedern. Hier werden täglich Links zu angesagten Fake-Sneakern geteilt.
Die führen etwa zur Marketplace-App "Hacoo", auf der zahlreiche, vor allem chinesische Händler replizierte Luxusprodukte anbieten. Wer die App installiert, kann mit wenigen Klicks Modelle von Prada, Louis Vuitton, Dior oder limitierte Nike-Sneaker bestellen - oft für gerade einmal 40 Euro inklusive Versand, während das Original auf Resale-Märkten locker 1.000 Euro kostet.
Influencer werben aktiv für Fälschungen
Neben solchen Gruppen machen auch viele Influencer und Content-Creator gezielt Werbung für Fake-Ware. Sie stellen sogenannte Spreadsheets vor: Das sind öffentlich einsehbare Tabellen, die wie Verkaufskataloge aufgebaut sind, erklärt der Sneaker-Experte Blumenthal. Dort können Käufer direkt Sneaker, Designeruhren oder Kleidung auswählen und werden zum jeweiligen Hersteller oder Agenten weitergeleitet.
Auf Plattformen wie OOPBUY, SUPERBUY oder ACBUY lassen sich über solche Spreadsheets Repliken bestellen. Da viele dieser Plattformen nicht direkt nach Europa liefern, übernehmen die Shopping-Agenten die Rolle des Zwischenhändlers. Angeboten werden auch sehr rare Modelle wie der Jordan 4 "OFF WHITE" oder der "Union - Guava Ice" als Fakes - für weniger als 100 Dollar, während Originale im Netz mit teils mehr als 6.000 Euro gehandelt werden.
"Schädigen den Ruf unserer Marke"
Auf Anfrage der ECHT-Redaktion zum Umgang damit äußert sich Nike nicht. Adidas schreibt in einer Stellungnahme: "Adidas schützt und verteidigt seine Markenrechte rigoros; dabei gehen wir schwerpunktmäßig gegen Händler und Importeure gefälschter Produkte als auch gegen sogenannte Fakeshops vor."
Dafür arbeite man auch eng mit zuständigen Behörden zusammen, da Fälschungen "aus minderwertigen oder sogar gesundheitsgefährdenden Materialien bestehen" könnten. "Sie schädigen den Ruf unserer Marke, unserer Partner und unserer Beschäftigten, die unermüdlich an der Erforschung und Entwicklung technischer Innovationen und kreativer Designs arbeiten."
Besitz ist in Deutschland nicht strafbar
Wer solche Produkte kauft, bewegt sich rein rechtlich in Deutschland in einer Grauzone: Für den privaten Gebrauch ist Besitz und Kauf in der Regel nicht strafbar. Problematisch wird es beim Handel: Dabei drohen Beschlagnahmung, Vernichtung der Ware und zivilrechtliche Schritte durch Markeninhaber wie beispielsweise Nike oder Adidas.
Praktisch dürften "Fake-Käufer" - rein statistisch gesehen - nicht viel zu befürchten haben. Rund 5,9 Milliarden Pakete mit geringem Warenwert kamen 2025 in der Europäischen Union an, das sind rund 16 Millionen Warensendungen pro Tag. Angesichts dieser Zahlen wird klar, dass nur wenige Sendungen tatsächlich durch den Zoll kontrolliert werden.
"Türkisches Original"
Neben China ist die Türkei ein wichtiger Hotspot für die Produktion von nachgemachten Markenprodukten. Rund zwölf Prozent aller Plagiate kommen aus der Türkei. In Istanbul, einer der größten Textilmetropolen Europas, reicht denn auch ein Blick in die Schaufenster voll günstiger Sneaker oft aus, um Fake Sneaker zu finden. Verkäufer sprechen vom "türkischen Original".
Emre ist einer dieser Basarverkäufer. Er erzählt, dass sie hier durchaus auch Besuch von Markenanwälten und der Polizei bekommen: "Die Anwälte der Markenhersteller kommen und checken, was verkauft wird. Wenn sie was finden, nehmen sie es mit und rufen die Polizei."
Billige Shoppingtour in Istanbul?
Fakes sind allgegenwärtig in der Türkei, denn sie werden auch vor Ort produziert, wie etwa in einer Fabrik außerhalb Istanbuls. Dort riecht es intensiv nach Kleber, überall stehen Kartons, Türen und Gitter, die Atmosphäre ist gedrückt. Eine Produzentin gibt offen zu: "Der weiße Turnschuh ist ein Fake. Ich habe den produziert." Auf die Frage, warum ihre Ware so günstig ist, antwortet sie: "Es ist nur ein kleiner Material- und Qualitätsunterschied. Die Klebestellen halten genauso lange wie beim Original."
Am Ende kostet dieser Schuh auf dem Basar in der türkischen Hauptstadt 16 Euro. Deshalb nutzen viele Urlauber eine Reise in die Türkei auch zum Shoppen. Wer aus dem Urlaub Fakes für den Privatgebrauch mitbringt, der muss in Deutschland in der Regel keine Strafe fürchten.
Außer, dass sie beschlagnahmt werden können. 2024 hat der deutsche Zoll über fünf Millionen Fakes im Wert von 417 Millionen Euro einbehalten. Und in einigen Ländern kann der Kauf von Fakes teuer werden - in Italien sind sogar bis zu 7.000 Euro Strafe möglich.
Schuhe von schlechter Qualität
Und nicht nur finanziell kann der Kauf von Fälschungen ein Risiko sein, auch gesundheitlich. ECHT? hat für die Recherche einige nachgemachte Sneaker gekauft und sie im Prüf- und Forschungsinstitut PFI in Pirmasens untersuchen lassen. Das Institut gilt als eine der etabliertesten Prüfstellen der Schuhbranche.
Die Ergebnisse sind ernüchternd: Der Fake-Adidas "Campus" zeigt zu hohen Abrieb, das Material bildet Löcher, auch im nassen Zustand, und starke Knotenbildung, so Diplom-Ingenieur Kai Tinschert, der die Tests durchgeführt hat. Auch die anderen Fake-Sneaker fallen im Test durch. Beim Nike-Fake "Air Force CPFM" bricht die Laufsohle im Test vollständig - "katastrophal" lautet das Urteil.
Gefährliche Schadstoffe in Fakes
Noch brisanter sind die Ergebnisse der Schadstoffanalyse. In einem Nike-Fake wird ein Lösemittel gefunden, Dimethylformamid, das häufig zur Herstellung synthetischer Materialien verwendet wird. "Dimethylformamid ist ein starkes Gift. Es führt zu Reizungen und ist lebertoxisch", erklärt die Chemie-Expertin Ines Anderie.
Das Problem daran ist: Solche Stoffe gasen aus den Schuhen aus, "selbst wenn man die auf die Terrasse stellt und länger auslüften lässt", so Anderie. "Wenn man die wieder reinholt ins Zimmer, dann wird das immer weiter ausgasen." Betroffen sind aber nicht nur Käufer, sondern vor allem die Beschäftigten in den Fabriken, die täglich mit diesen Chemikalien arbeiten.
Auch im Fake-Adidas "Samba" werden Schadstoffe gefunden, konkret ein verbotener Weichmacher: DEHP. Der Grenzwert ist überschritten, der Schuh dürfte in Deutschland gar nicht verkauft werden. Expertin Anderie erklärt: "Diese Substanzen haben hormonaktive Wirkung. Sie können die Fortpflanzung beeinträchtigen, das Kind im Mutterleib schädigen und im schlimmsten Fall Krebs auslösen." Die vermeintlichen Schnäppchen können also mit erheblichen Gesundheitsrisiken belastet sein.
Gefälschte Waren erkennen
Um Käufer davor zu schützen, dass sie wie Christopher Blumenthal versehentlich gefälschte Waren kaufen, bieten Dienste wie "LegitGrails" eine Authentifizierung per App an. Nutzer laden Detailfotos ihrer Schuhe hoch, die von geschulten Experten und unterstützender KI geprüft werden.
Das Unternehmen wirbt mit einer Genauigkeit von 99,89 Prozent. Auch die vier im Labor untersuchten Fälschungen hat die App innerhalb von 30 Minuten klar als Fälschungen erkannt - trotz ihres hochwertigen Aussehens.

title: Росіяни вдарили по Дніпру: пошкоджені будинки, під завалами можуть бути люди
content_c:
Росіяни вдарили по Дніпру: пошкоджені будинки, під завалами можуть бути люди
Унаслідок російської атаки на Дніпро пошкоджено приватні будинки. Постраждала 84-річна жінка, яку госпіталізували. Є побоювання, що в пошкоджених оселях залишилися заблоковані люди.
Російські війська завдали удару по Дніпру 19 жовтня. Внаслідок атаки пошкоджено приватні житлові будинки. За попередньою інформацією, всередині можуть перебувати заблоковані люди.
Про це повідомив начальник Дніпропетровської ОВА Олександр Ганжа.
За його словами, внаслідок російського удару постраждала 84-річна жінка. Медики доправили її до лікарні для надання необхідної допомоги.
Також очільник області повідомив про пошкодження приватних будинків.
«За попередньою інформацією, у них можуть бути заблоковані люди», — зазначив Ганжа.
На місці атаки працюють усі необхідні екстрені служби.
Наразі інформація про масштаби руйнувань та можливу кількість людей, які залишаються в пошкоджених будинках, уточнюється.
Нагадаємо, що у Києві після атаки РФ закрили дві станції метро: як курсуватимуть поїзди

title: Премьер-министр Албании обвинил Россию и Иран во вмешательстве в антиправительственные протесты
content_c:
Премьер-министр Албании Эди Рама обвинил спецслужбы России и Ирана в содействии антиправительственным протестам в стране. По его мнению, беспорядки могут стать препятствием на пути Албании к вступлению в ЕС.
«У нас есть множество доказательств иностранного вмешательства. За масками скрываются те, кто желает Албании зла и хочет заполучить ее исключительно для себя», — заявил глава правительства, обвинив «иностранные силы», в частности Россию и Иран, во вмешательстве в протесты, пишет Bloomberg.
В Албании с лета продолжались протесты против застройки острова Сазан и прилегающих прибрежных территорий. К проекту привлечена инвестиционная компания Affinity Partners, основанная в 2021 году Джаредом Кушнером — зятем президента США Дональда Трампа. Протестующие опасаются, что строительство курортного комплекса нанесет ущерб лагуне Вйоса-Нарта и району Звернеца, где обитают перелетные птицы, в частности фламинго.
В июле 2026 года депутаты Европейского парламента предупреждали, что продвижение курортного проекта без надлежащей защиты природоохранных территорий может поставить под угрозу переговоры о вступлении Албании в ЕС. В октябре протесты переросли в более широкие антиправительственные выступления, участники которых начали требовать отставки Рамы, критикуя власти также за коррупцию, безработицу и проблемы в сфере образования.
За последние пять дней протестов пострадали 272 человека, в том числе 169 полицейских, 82 участника акций и 21 прохожий.
Напомним, во Франции протесты из-за условий в школах переросли в движение против неравенства, сокращения государственных расходов и удорожания жизни. В субботу они охватили Париж, Лион, Марсель, Бордо и Лилль, а в Лиможе огонь уничтожил крышу исторической ратуши.

title: 'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
content_c:
'Very upsetting': Residents in shock after historic French town hall set alight
A historic town hall in the French city of Limoges has been damaged in an apparent arson attack following a day of nationwide protests on Saturday.
Dramatic footage shared online shows the 19th-century building engulfed in flames, with the spire of its clock tower later collapsing.
On Sunday, stunned residents watched as firefighters, who had battled the blaze through the night, assessed the building's structural integrity. Officials have not yet confirmed whether the town hall is at risk of collapse.
"Damaging heritage buildings because you're angry with the government is selfish", one resident told the BBC.
BBC correspondent Chris Bockman reports from Limoges.

title: Guardian reporter filmed masked militants seconds before West Bank attack on French mayor
content_c:
Hours after Israeli militants attacked a delegation of European diplomats, French clerics and a visiting mayor in the occupied West Bank, Israel’s leader, Benjamin Netanyahu, responded by questioning the delegation’s account of the assault.
“Serious accusations require serious evidence” was the all-caps headline of a social media post from the office of the prime minister. As news of the attack spread globally there was no pledge to find those accountable and bring them to justice.
Instead Netanyahu’s team dismissed video of Bernard Baudoux, the mayor of Aulnoye-Aymeries in northern France, on the ground grimacing in pain and shock, photos of the smashed window of a diplomatic car, and footage of masked men threatening diplomats and activists with sticks.
“These images alone do not establish the complete sequence of events or individual responsibility,” the statement said, warning of “concerns about a coordinated campaign to smear Israel”.
The prime minister’s office went on to cast doubt on the integrity of senior French, Belgian and Polish diplomats in Jerusalem and clergy from the Catholic church who witnessed and reported the attack.
“We call on the public and responsible journalists to demand verifiable evidence, reject hearsay and refuse to turn unproven allegations into a collective indictment of the Jewish residents of Judea and Samaria [the occupied West Bank],” it said.
Guardian footage
Footage below filmed by the Guardian (no audio) shows the moments before Israeli settlers attacked the French mayor Bernard Baudoux, who was in the Palestinian town of Taybeh with a delegation of European diplomats. A second clip shows the immediate aftermath of the attack. The final section shows one group of settlers attacking the car carrying Baudoux and others.
Verifying the details of attacks can be painstaking journalistic work, seeking out eyewitness accounts, photos and videos for confirmation.
But this weekend the Guardian was in Taybeh, and witnessed the masked militants speeding up a hill in order to attack diplomats and French visitors who had spent a morning peacefully harvesting olives with Palestinians who own the groves.
Shortly after 1pm, they were warned that settlers had attacked Palestinians harvesting olives nearby. Keen to avoid confrontation, the group decided to leave and were approaching their vehicles as the militants closed in, masked, menacing and brandishing sticks.
The Guardian filmed the moments before Baudoux was assaulted, showing him approaching an SUV with his wife and Vincent Dollmann, the archbishop of Cambrai, escorted by diplomatic security. Our vehicle pulled away, making room for the two parked by the road to follow.
Moments later the settlers attacked, apparently determined not only to force the foreigners to flee but to extract a price for joining Palestinians on their land.
It was clear the group contained foreign dignitaries because the cars had diplomatic plates, and Baudoux was apparently targeted for his nationality, because he was wearing his mayor’s sash of office. One of the attackers aggressively shouted “France, France” before pushing him to the ground, eyewitnesses said.
Metadata from that video shows there were just 22 seconds between the last shot of Baudoux remonstrating with his attackers and footage of him slumped on the ground taken by activists in the second car.
The embassy security team then helped him into the vehicle but the attack continued as they drove off. Footage filmed from the hillside opposite shows the settlers attacking the SUV as pulls away.
The force of their blows smashed one of the reinforced windows at the back of the car, which can be seen intact in the first video. A photo of the crumpled pane taken minutes later in the relative safety of Taybeh shows the force of the impact.
If the militant settlers had broken one of the windows next to the passengers, it is unlikely those inside would have escaped injuries.
